Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) 
may further accelerate the rational design of g-C₃N₄-
based nanoplatforms [138]. AI-assisted approaches could 
integrate synthesis parameters, structural descriptors, 
optical properties, catalytic activity, ROS profiles, cellular 
responses, and toxicity data to identify relationships that 
are difficult to derive from conventional trial-and-error 
approaches. Predictive models may facilitate optimiza­
tion of dopant concentration, defect density, heterojunc­
tion composition, particle size, and surface chemistry. 
However, the usefulness of AI models will depend on the 
quality, standardization, and comparability of the under­
lying experimental datasets. Establishing interoperable 
datasets and standardized characterization and biologi­
cal-assessment protocols will therefore be an important 
prerequisite for reliable AI-guided nanomaterial design.

Conclusion
Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C₃N₄)-based smart nano­
platforms have emerged as a transformative class of 
nanomaterials for next-generation cancer therapy. Their 
unique combination of metal-free composition, tunable 
electronic structure, excellent photostability, favorable 
biocompatibility, and versatile surface chemistry makes 
them highly promising candidates for precision oncology. 
Recent advances in surface engineering including hetero­
atom doping, heterojunction construction, noble metal 
decoration, oxygen vacancy engineering, and biomimetic 
surface functionalization have substantially enhanced 
the photocatalytic performance of g-C₃N₄ by improv­
ing light harvesting, accelerating charge separation and 
amplifying reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. 
Beyond conventional photodynamic therapy, g-C₃N₄-
based nanoplatforms have evolved into multifunctional

Cardiovascular and neurological disease together impose one of the largest preventable disease
burdens in India, yet every application-specific integrated circuit used in the cardiac and neurological
monitoring devices sold domestically is currently imported. This paper presents CardioNeural-SoC, an

signal processing core with hardware accelerators for arrhythmia and seizure-onset classification, an
